abstract: Federated speech emotion recognition (SER) is challenged by speaker-dependent, class-imbalanced data and by heterogeneous client devices. This paper proposes \textit{Fuzzy-FedAvg}, a server-aware framework in which the server learns Client Selection Weights (CSWs) through fuzzy Q-learning from global-model feedback. The same CSWs weight client accuracy, training time, and \divkpi{} in both client selection and aggregation, while a dedicated PCAS node manages stragglers through staleness-discounted deferred updates. On IEMOCAP and CREMA-D, \textit{Fuzzy-FedAvg} achieves higher unweighted average recall (UAR) than FedAvg in all configurations under severe non-IID conditions, and in 22 of 24 participation-level and 10 of 12 training-horizon configurations overall. It also outperforms FedProx and Oort, while SCAFFOLD and Power-of-Choice remain competitive, and it reduces cumulative training time by 81.2\% in a FedScale-based evaluation. The benefit is greatest under strong statistical heterogeneity and narrows as data become more balanced.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对说话人差异大且设备快慢不一的联邦语音情感识别，Fuzzy-FedAvg 让服务器从全局反馈中学习三类指标的权重，用同一组权重同时指导选谁参与和更新如何融合，在严重非独立同分布下提升平均召回并大幅缩短累积训练时间，但最差客户端性能并未系统性改善。
originalTitle: Fuzzy-FedAvg: Server-Aware Client Selection for Federated Speech Emotion Recognition in Heterogeneous Environments
readerTitle: 服务器如何学会挑选客户端：Fuzzy-FedAvg 在非独立同分布语音情感识别中的做法
